name: City Council Meeting
minutes_text:
MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Agency,
  Community Development Financing Authority,
  Public Improvement Corporation,
  and Library Board of Trustees*

  April 6, 2009

A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Agency, the Community
Development Financing Authority, the Public Improvement Corporation, and the Library Board
of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor Ury at 5:04
p.m., on April 6, 2009 at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted
by 5:00 p.m. on April 1, 2009, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. Copies were also
posted at the Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive, and the
Norman P. Murray Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

Present:  Council Member Kelley (arrived at 5:07 p.m.)
  Council Member Ledesma
  Council Member Schlicht
  Mayor Pro Tem MacLean
  Mayor Ury

Absent:  None

Staff Present:  Irwin B. Bornstein, Assistant City Manager/Director of Admin. Services
  William P. Curley III, City Attorney
  Karen Hamman, City Clerk

Staff Absent:  Dennis Wilberg, City Manager

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Mayor Pro Tem MacLean

INVOCATION: Mayor Ury

CLOSED SESSION

REPORT OF CLOSED SESSION

City Council Minutes  1  April 6, 2009
 RECESS

  Mayor Ury declared a recess at 5:05 p.m. The City Council reconvened at 6:00 p.m. with
  all five Council Members present.

PRESENTATIONS

P1.  Tree City USA Award

  Shannon Johnson, California Department of Forestry and Fire Protection, presented
  Mayor Ury with the 2009 Tree City USA Award.

P2.  Proclaim April 25, 2009, to be "Artes de la Vida" and "Earth Day Expo"

  Community Services Supervisor Virginia Chavez invited residents to the Artes de la Vida
  and Earth Day Expo events on April 25, 2009, at Oso Viejo Park on the Village Green.
  Ms. Chavez requested that those attending bring a canned food donation for the local
  food banks.

PUBLIC COMMENTS

  Larry Gilbert, M.V.: expressed dissatisfaction that the City did not have records
  responsive to his request for Mission Hospital’s expansion-related sales and use taxes as
  projected in the Development Agreement.

  Joyce Saltzgiver, President of the Casta del Sol Homeowners Association, M.V.:
  announced her concern that those gathering signatures in the effort to recall Mayor Pro
  Tem MacLean do not know the potential cost of an election should the recall be
  successful.

  Kime Goodrum, M.V.: stated that he has recently had difficulty getting a tennis court at
  the Marguerite Recreation Center and while more and more court time is taken away,
  dues have not dropped.

  David Corrich, M.V.: discussed cell reception problems in his neighborhood and
  presented the City Clerk with a survey of Pacific Hills residents who request the
  installation of cell sites on the existing light poles at Gilleran Park.

CONSENT CALENDAR

Items 6, 8, 10, and 11 were removed from the Consent Calendar for separate discussion.

City Council Minutes  2  April 6, 2009
 Motion made by Council Member Ledesma, seconded by Council Member Kelley, to approve
the Consent Calendar as described below.

On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

AYES:  Kelley, Ledesma, MacLean, Schlicht, and Ury
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  None

1.  Waive Reading of Ordinances and Resolutions

  Approved the reading by title of all ordinances and resolutions and declared that said
  titles which appear on the public agenda shall be determined to have been read by title
  and further reading waived.

2.  City Council Minutes

  Approved the Minutes for the City Council Meeting of March 16, 2009, as presented.

3.  Check Register dated March 6, 2009, in the amount of $434,555.45

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

4.  Check Register dated March 13, 2009, in the amount of $644,546.89

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

5.  Check Register dated March 20, 2009, in the amount of $873,919.11

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

7.  Montanoso and Sierra Recreation Centers Tennis Court Lights Replacement
  Project (CIP 316)

  (1) Certified the completion of and accepted the improvements for the subject property;
  (2) authorized the City Manager to sign the Notice of Completion; (3) authorized the City
  Clerk to record the Notice of Completion with the County of Orange and to release the
  faithful performance and payment bonds one year and 35 days respectively after the date
  of recordation of the Notice of Completion contingent upon no claims or liens being filed

City Council Minutes  3  April 6, 2009
   with or by the City; and (4) authorized the payment of the final retention of $16, 840.00
  35 days after the date of recordation of the Notice of Completion.

9.  2009 Residential Resurfacing (CIP 838)

  Approved the bid specifications and authorized staff to advertise for construction bids for
  the subject project.

PUBLIC HEARINGS

OLD BUSINESS

NEW BUSINESS

ITEMS REMOVED FROM THE CONSENT CALENDAR

6.  Selection of Independent Auditor for Fiscal Years Ending June 30, 2009 and June
  30, 2010

  Council Member Schlicht inquired about additional audits anticipated by staff and what
  new accounting standards are expected in the future.

  Motion was made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem MacLean, to
  award a contract to Mayer Hoffman McCann P.C. to serve as the City’s independent
  auditors for fiscal years ending June 30, 2009 and June 30, 2010, at a cost not to exceed
  $73,870 ($36,390 for FY 2008-09 and $37,480 for FY 2009-10) for the annual financial
  statement audit work.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Ledesma, MacLean, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

8.  Oso Creek Trail Signage (CIP 317)

  Council Member Schlicht announced that she would be voting against this item because
  she feels it is a waste of Federal funding and a gross expenditure.

  Motion was made by Council Member Ledesma, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem MacLean,
  to approve the contract documents and authorize staff to advertise for bids.

City Council Minutes  4  April 6, 2009
   On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Ledesma, MacLean, and Ury
  NOES:  Schlicht
  ABSENT:  None

10.  Mission Viejo Chamber of Commerce April Membership Mixer

  Council Member Schlicht stated that she is not against adult beverages but she is against
  the Social Host Ordinance previously adopted by the City Council. She will be voting no
  on this item because she fees it is disingenuous to support both concepts.

  Motion was made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem MacLean, to
  approve the request by the Mission Viejo Chamber of Commerce for an exemption to the
  "No Alcoholic Beverage Consumption" regulation for the April Chamber Mixer
  scheduled for Wednesday, April 22, 2009, in the Kershaw Garden and City Hall
  Saddleback Room.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Ledesma, MacLean, and Ury
  NOES:  Schlicht
  ABSENT:  None

11.  Destruction of Records - Citywide 2007-08 Records Purge

  By consensus, the Council expressed an interest in retaining a copy of all City Council
  Meeting videotapes and directed staff not to destroy any videotapes without prior
  approval of the City Council.

  Motion was made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Council Member Ledesma,
  to adopt Resolution 2009-09 Authorizing and Directing the City Clerk to Destroy Certain
  City Records and Documents Pursuant to the Government Code of the State of
  California.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Ledesma, MacLean, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

City Council Minutes  5  April 6, 2009
 MAYOR’S, COMMISSION, AND COMMITTEE REPORTS

12.  Norman P. Murray Community and Senior Center Room Rental Rates

  Director of Recreation and Community Services Kelly Doyle presented the staff report
  and outlined the recommendation of the Community Services Commission.

  The following expressed opposition to a fee increase in private party rental rates for
  Mission Viejo residents: Larry Gilbert, M.V. and Mark Dobrilovic.

  Motion was made by Council Member Ledesma, seconded by Council Member Kelley,
  to deny the recommended action.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Ledesma, MacLean, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

13.  Orange County Fire Authority (OCFA) Report

  Received the report from Council Member Kelley.

14.  Foothill/Eastern Transportation Corridor Agency Report

  Received the report from Mayor Pro Tem MacLean.

15.  San Joaquin Hills Transportation Corridor Agency Report

  Council Member Ledesma announced that he did not attend the last meeting of the San
  Joaquin Hills TCA.

16.  Discussion Regarding Mission Viejo and its Compliance with Housing Laws

  City Attorney Bill Curley announced that staff had hoped to bring something forward at
  this meeting but they have been unable to coordinate schedules and plan to return to the
  Council at the next meeting instead.

17.  Roundabout Intersections Committee Report

  Received the report from Council Member Schlicht.

City Council Minutes  6  April 6, 2009
 18.  SCAG Transportation & Communications Committee (TCC) Report

  Received the report from Council Member Kelley.

STAFF REPORTS

City Manager's Report

City Attorney’s Report

19.  Elections Code 9219 Report and an Action by the City Council to Either: Adopt an
  Ordinance Titled "Right to Vote Amendment;" or to Set the Initiative Ordinance
  for Vote at the Next General Election; or Take No Action or Consider a Legal
  Challenge of the Proposed Initiative Ordinance

  City Attorney Bill Curley presented the staff report.

  Motion was made by Mayor Pro Tem MacLean, seconded by Council Member Kelley, to
  submit the ordinance to the voters at the next regular municipal election that is to be held
  not less than 88 days after the date of the order (this is anticipated to be June 8, 2010).

  Mayor Ury departed at 7:38 p.m. and returned at 7:39 p.m.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Ledesma, MacLean, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

  Council Member Ledesma stated for the record that he did not agendaize this item, nor
  did he second the motion to adopt the ordinance. He did not donate money to circulate
  petitions for this initiative, he did not circulate the petitions himself, nor did he ever sign
  the petition to move this initiative forward.

COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS

20.  Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended

  The City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities calendars as
  presented in the staff report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk for the
  public record.

City Council Minutes  7  April 6, 2009
 Council Member Kelley

  Council Member Kelley provided an update on economic development activities. There
  has not been a recent meeting of the ad hoc committee however she discussed her efforts
  to contact brokers who have shopping center vacancies in an attempt to find out what
  they are doing to attract retailers or restaurants to their sites and if there is anything the
  City can do to assist. She will bring some ideas to the committee in the near future and
  the committee will consider a service similar to the Buxton proposal, but from a company
  that has offered a markedly reduced price. Council Member Kelley invited residents to
  several upcoming family events: Bunny Days on Saturday, April 11, Artes de la Vida on
  April 25, Fun With Chalk on May 2 and 3, and the Relay for Life on June 6 and 7, 2009.
  She invited anyone interested in joining a Relay for Life team to visit www.mvrelay.org
  for more information. Council Member Kelley announced that the Community of
  Character word for the month of April is service. She further discussed the recent public
  notice regarding water and sewer rate increases and she announced that there will be a
  public hearing for Moulton Niguel Water District (MNWD) customers on May 26, 2009
  at 6:00 p.m. at the District headquarters. Council Member Kelley has also invited
  MNWD to come to a City Council Meeting to make a public presentation on the
  proposed water and sewer rate increases.

Council Member Ledesma

  Council Member Ledesma stated that he looks forward to attending the Bunny Days
  event this Saturday and he stated that the water situation is another example of
  preservation of tiny fish in the Sacramento delta.

Council Member Schlicht

  Council Member Schlicht apologized to Council Member Kelley for coming across
  harshly when discussing the allowance of alcohol at community events earlier this
  evening. She wished residents a good week entering into Passover and Easter.

Mayor Pro Tem MacLean

  Mayor Pro Tem MacLean announced that he and Mayor Ury attended the League of
  Cities Transportation, Communication and Public Works Policy Committee meeting in
  Los Angeles last Friday. He provided an outline of the legislative changes that affect
  transportation and the action the Committee took to support or oppose specific bills. He
  announced that Richard (Dick) O’Neill recently passed away and he asked Mayor Ury to
  adjourn tonight’s meeting in Mr. O’Neill’s memory. Mayor Pro Tem MacLean
  commented on the recall efforts against him and referred to the observations made by a
  member of the public earlier this evening. He stated that there is a group of individuals
  who claim, under the banner of integrity and transparency in government, that a recall is
  warranted yet they do the exact opposite by telling variations of the truth or outright lies

City Council Minutes  8  April 6, 2009
   while trying to gather signatures on the recall petition. Mayor Pro Tem MacLean
  encouraged anyone with concerns to contact him at city hall or by email. He stated that
  he is happy to answer questions and he can provide documents and reliable sources to
  verify anything he says.

Mayor Ury

  Mayor Ury stated that the updates have been thorough this evening and he reminded
  residents to make sure they don't miss Bunny Days on Saturday.

ADJOURNMENT

  At the hour of 8:20 p.m., there being no further business to come before the City Council
  at this session, Mayor Ury adjourned the meeting in memory of Richard O'Neill to
  Monday, April 20, 2009, at 5:00 p.m.

__________________________________________
Karen Hamman, City Clerk

Approved at the meeting of April 20, 2009

City Council Minutes  9  April 6, 2009
